abstract: We present the case of a 30-year-old man with no prior medical history who presented to the hospital with a myriad of symptoms such as shortness of breath, generalized weakness, lower limb weakness, and urinary retention. He was recently diagnosed with "disseminated coccidioidomycosis" by an outside provider on an outpatient basis and started on fluconazole orally. However, due to a lack of improvement and significant symptoms, he was sent to the hospital to initiate liposomal amphotericin B treatment. After a comprehensive workup, an alternative diagnosis was suspected and eventually confirmed as metastatic germ cell carcinoma. Due to the vast dissemination and his poor functional status despite chemotherapy initiation, the patient elected for palliative care and expired shortly after at hospice. This case demonstrates the similarity of clinical findings between disseminated infections and malignancies.
abstract_ja: 30歳で既往歴のない男性が、呼吸困難、全身倦怠感、下肢脱力感、および尿閉などの多くの症状を呈して入院した。彼は最近、外来で「播種性コクシジオイデス菌症」と診断され、フルコナゾールの経口投与を開始されていた。しかし、改善がなく、症状が著しいため、彼は入院してリポソームアンホテリシンB治療を開始された。包括的な検査の後、別の診断が疑われ、最終的に転移性胚細胞癌と確認された。広範な転移とそれに関わらず化学療法開始後も不良なパフォーマンスステータスのため、患者は緩和ケアを選択し、その直後にホスピスで死亡した。本症例は、播種性感染症と悪性腫瘍の臨床所見の類似性を示している。
